races.name: Tom Halliday Memorial Conditional Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Bannister
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner on OR 100 and the pick of the staying form on good ground (2nd over 18f, 1W5P in similar conditions), Tom Broughton takes the ride for Nick Kent who has not struck in 3 attempts in the last 14 days; 234 days off the track is the significant question mark, though the good-going record and class give him a chance if fit.|

runners_data.name: Oneinthewell
runners_data.note: James Owen's five-year-old holds an OR of 99 and good form at 16-20f, though all five recent runs have come on soft or heavy and this good ground is an unproven surface — the going-change is the biggest doubt and the lengthy 146-day absence compounds it.|

runners_data.name: Lakefield Flyer
runners_data.note: Won over this trip on good ground last time and has an excellent 14/15 similar-going strike-rate for John Joseph Hanlon; only five days since his last run is notably fresh, and while his natural instinct is to race from behind, he is one of the hold-up horses bumped forward on the map — his chances hinge on securing a better position than a true hold-up style would suggest.|

runners_data.name: William Of York
runners_data.note: A ten-year-old on a concerning recent sequence of UP-06P and with just 0W1P on good ground from 15 starts in similar conditions; Charlie Maggs partners for Rebecca Menzies and, while he is the map's sole prominent type behind the leader, the form gives little confidence he can sustain a challenge.|

runners_data.name: Captain Connor
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with only soft/heavy ground runs in his history, so this good ground is an unknown — all four runs in that going description (UNKNOWN base) and a mark of 89 suggest talent, but his natural race from the rear means he is squeezed into a midfield slot that does not suit, and the STYLE_FIT discount applies.|

runners_data.name: Gone In Sixty
runners_data.note: The race's lone front-runner with a superb 13/15 record on good ground and multiple placed efforts at Market Rasen; Alex Hales's conditional booking is notable but does not undermine a horse whose entire tactical advantage is the absence of any challenger willing to take him on — this is his race to lose.|

runners_data.name: Makinbecon
runners_data.note: Barry John Murphy's six-year-old ran third over 18f on good ground just 12 days ago (good strike-rate 3/7) and has the freshest legs in the field; a genuine hold-up performer by nature, he finds himself pushed into a midfield map slot, meaning Callum Pritchard must make a decision early about whether to commit forward or settle and hope.|

runners_data.name: Time Was
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's nine-year-old has 0W1P on good ground from six similar-going runs and recent form of 434-P8 is uninspiring; Oscar Palmer takes a 3lb claim, which marginally offsets the weight, but this horse's true racing style is from behind and the redistribution note means he is unlikely to find an uncontested position — hard to see him featuring.|

races.paceDynamic: Gone In Sixty is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to press him from the outset, Rian Corcoran should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop across the 2m4½f trip on good ground at Market Rasen. His strong course-and-distance profile (13 of 15 runs on good ground, multiple placed efforts over 20f here) means he is no bluffer up front — he can set an honest but manageable pace that keeps the field strung out without burning himself off. William Of York is the only other horse nominally drawn as prominent, but his recent form figures of UP-06P and modest good-going record suggest he is unlikely to pressurise Gone In Sixty meaningfully. This race shape — a lone, uncontested front-runner on good ground over a staying trip — classically rewards horses with the tactical versatility to travel close to the pace from an early stage rather than deep hold-up specialists, yet a sustainable tempo also leaves the door ajar for a powerful finisher if the front-runner ties up late; the field holds more genuine hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear, with Lakefield Flyer, Captain Connor, Makinbecon and Time Was all true hold-up horses redistributed to midfield positions they may struggle to occupy naturally, making Bannister and Oneinthewell — both shown at hold-up but running from higher ratings with better going form — the most likely challengers if the pace softens enough in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Gone In Sixty Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Gone In Sixty bowls along in front at a steady-to-honest clip and no rival has the inclination or ability to close the gap turning in.
scenarios.body: Gone In Sixty's class edge (OR 84 but with 13/15 good-ground runs) and Alex Hales's booking of a conditional should not mask a horse who has placed repeatedly in this grade on this going; unchallenged, he can slow the race to his own rhythm and find enough from the last flight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fast enough to expose Gone In Sixty in the final quarter-mile and a finisher times a challenge from the straight to overhaul him.
scenarios.body: Bannister (OR 100, good-going form 2/18f, 1W5P in similar conditions) or Oneinthewell (OR 99, versatile trip) could be the beneficiary if the front-runner's lead evaporates after the second-last; both carry top weights but have the class to absorb that if the race sets up as a true stamina test.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Challenges
scenarios.trigger: If William Of York or a redistributed hold-up horse manages to travel prominently and picks off Gone In Sixty from his shoulder in the straight.
scenarios.body: Lakefield Flyer has the best good-going record of the redistributed group (2W7P in similar conditions, recent course-distance win) and could find the position if the field fans out early; however, his STYLE_FIT discount (0.92) and the crowded midfield must be noted as meaningful risks.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Bunches, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If an early incident or crawl creates a falsely-run race and the whole field pours into the straight together.
scenarios.body: Makinbecon (1W2P on good ground, recent third over 18f) or Captain Connor could deliver a late rattle if chaos scrambles the normal tactical order, but both are tagged redistributed with STYLE_FIT discounts and this scenario depends on atypical race development.

watchPoints.text: Gone In Sixty — watch whether Rian Corcoran goes fully unchallenged to the front at the first flight; if William Of York or Lakefield Flyer crowds him early, the pace dynamic changes completely.

Lakefield Flyer — only five days since his last run, and if he arrives fresh and forward-travelling, he may naturally push into a more prominent position than his redistribution tag implies, making him a live danger to the favourite.

Bannister — 234 days off the track is a significant fitness risk for a nine-year-old; watch his coat and paddock demeanour, as a well-held-up run that fades after the last would suggest he needs the run.
Oneinthewell — all five recent runs on soft or softer; if the good ground rides quicker than expected and the pace is strong, his stamina may be tested in a way his recent form has not demanded.

Time Was and Captain Connor — both carrying redistribution and STYLE_FIT discounts with no proven good-ground form; if either is found wide and off the bridle early, they are unlikely to land a blow and can be dismissed from serious consideration.

races.name: Malton Marquees Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Boom Boom Boris
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist who has finished fourth twice over similar good ground, recording a fall in latest run (3/3F-4); Harry Bannister knows this horse's habits but getting a clean passage from the rear in a small field over 2m4½f on Good will require the pace to be strong enough — last 33 days is fine.

runners_data.name: Brosna Town
runners_data.note: Returns after a 260-day absence (8F hurdle run omitted) and has headgear fitted (tongue-tie), with Conor Rabbitt (3) claiming; his best form has come at shorter, and the step up to 2m4½f on Good ground is the key unknown, though a prominent racing style suits the likely shape.

runners_data.name: Military Saint
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and carrying a significant question mark — last run was a point-to-point pulled-up effort (71P), no trainer 14-day data available, and the going preference is listed as unknown; the upside is entirely hidden, which makes him a speculative proposition despite OR=120.

runners_data.name: Way Maker
runners_data.note: Ran just seven days ago, which demands respect regarding recovery, but his trainer-jockey combination is potent (Mickey and James Bowen, 2/10 in 14 days) and his recent second over 2m Good ground plus a win at 2m show he handles these conditions; a prominent racing style perfectly fits the expected race shape.

runners_data.name: Rogue Impact
runners_data.note: Only one career hurdle run recorded (second at 2m, Good), so this 2m4½f trip is a significant step into the unknown; Jonathan Burke is a reliable partner but his hold-up style means he needs either a strong pace or a flat-out sprint finish to pick up, and neither is guaranteed in this small field.

runners_data.name: Lipstick Traces
runners_data.note: Consistent placed form across a variety of trips and conditions but a genuine hold-up horse here shuffled into midfield on the pace map because the rear is crowded — her natural position is further back than shown, so she races in a compromised role and the STYLE_FIT flag (0.90) appropriately tempers confidence; Callum Bewley will need luck in running from off the pace.

runners_data.name: Little Lady Rock
runners_data.note: The race's lone front-runner and will set the tempo unchallenged, though three consecutive seconds at shorter trips (16-17f, Good) suggests she finds one or two too good at the business end; the step up in trip here may actually suit, and controlling the race from the front with Ben Poste aboard is her most obvious platform.

races.paceDynamic: Little Lady Rock is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with only seven runners in a maiden hurdle, she will set a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset — there is no rival to pressure her into an uncharacteristic tempo. Way Maker and Brosna Town are the prominent types most likely to track her into second and third on the fence, giving this race a clean, processional shape through the early stages on Good ground over 2m4½f. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can place at the rear — Lipstick Traces is a genuine hold-up horse shifted into midfield on the map, but in practice she will likely be further back than shown, meaning the race shape genuinely compresses the field toward the front. A measured, front-runner-led tempo over this trip on Good ground strongly favours the prominent-to-lead profile: horses who travel close to the pace will dictate their own terms, while true hold-up runners face a stern test of finishing speed if the gallop never truly hotches up.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Little Lady Rock Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Little Lady Rock bowls clear unchallenged and sets a fair but unhurried pace that suits those tracking her.
scenarios.body: Little Lady Rock dictates from the front with Way Maker and Brosna Town close behind, and the race becomes a test of jumping accuracy and class rather than finishing speed; those who travel prominently have first run on the home turn.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Way Maker or Brosna Town move upsides Little Lady Rock entering the final half-mile and the pace quickens from the front.
scenarios.body: The complexion shifts into a genuine battle between the prominent trio inside the final six fences, suiting horses with a solid racing age and good jumping; Way Maker's recent good-ground form and course-appropriate trip make him the chief threat.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough that prominent horses tie up and a hold-up runner can close.
scenarios.body: Boom Boom Boris or Rogue Impact would need the race to be run at an unusually sharp tempo for a field this small, but if the front-runners overdo it, they carry enough class to finish powerfully; Rogue Impact is unexposed at this trip and could improve sharply.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse/Melee
scenarios.trigger: If the early tempo is so slow that the race turns into a sprint from the last and stamina counts for nothing.
scenarios.body: With just seven runners and one true front-runner, a crawl is possible if Little Lady Rock is steadied, turning the race into a hurdle-by-hurdle attritional test of jumping; Military Saint's lightly-raced profile and unknown ceiling could exploit chaos.

watchPoints.text: Watch Way Maker for any signs of fatigue or stiffness given his run just seven days ago — if he travels sweetly to two out he is the key threat to the leader, but a flat performance would be explained by the quick turnaround.

Monitor Little Lady Rock's jumping under pressure — she has never made the running in a field this competitive and any errors at the hurdles could open the door for Way Maker or Brosna Town to steal an advantage.

Brosna Town's layoff of 260 days (excluding a flat run) combined with the tongue-tie fitment and step up in trip are three simultaneous unknowns; a slow jumper or a blowout for fitness could compromise the jockey's ability to hold his prominent position.

Rogue Impact's trip record is limited entirely to 2m or shorter — watch how he travels in the back straight over 2m4½f Good, as any sign of labouring before the home turn would confirm the distance is beyond his current scope.

Military Saint's unknown going preference and point-to-point pulled-up run make him a surveillance horse — Tom Bellamy's early positioning will be informative: if he is allowed to bowl along in the first mile it suggests connections are confident, while a hold-up ride in a crawl invites trouble.

races.name: ECIS Say Yes To Solar Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Fidendum
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with a solid sim-going profile (1W2P on Good) and two of her last three runs producing a win and a placed effort over this exact course and distance; the 3lb claim from Nick Slatter is a meaningful asset, but she needs a run of daylight and enough early pace to close into — the headgear (hood/tongue tie) suggests a horse that needs managing.

runners_data.name: Granny Hawkins
runners_data.note: Has won three of her last four on Good ground at 2m½f and is the sole front-runner here, giving her full control of the tempo; the 77-day absence is a mild flag but Alan King's yard has sent out three winners from 11 runs in the last fortnight, and a STYLE_FIT score of 0.93 reflects that she is racing squarely within her role rather than out of it — she is the shape-setter.

runners_data.name: Tilehurst
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen takes the ride for Neil Mulholland, who has struck at 1 from 16 runners over the last 14 days; Tilehurst's consistent placed record (2-3-3-2-4 in last five) on Good ground at this trip gives her strong profile credentials for a pressers' race, and 92 days off the track is the only nagging concern.

runners_data.name: Kaikoura
runners_data.note: A 4-year-old who hasn't run for 267 days — the longest absence in this field — and whose form figures of 33075 include a fall and a seventh; the hold-up style suits a race with genuine pace, but the layoff, the youth, and a 0W3P sim-going record make this a significant unknown quantity under Nathan Moscrop.

runners_data.name: Diesel Line
runners_data.note: Charles & Adam Pogson's 8-year-old brings a 0 wins from 3 runs in the trainer's last 14 days, and the recent form ended with a fall last time out, which must be noted; his tongue-tie is fitted and his record shows he settles into prominent positions — he has the right tactical profile for this shape but is vulnerable to classier rivals over the final flight.

runners_data.name: Crown Of India
runners_data.note: Showed a 2-1 in the last two starts which looks eye-catching, but this is a hold-up horse whose natural inclination to race from the rear is compromised here — with Fidendum, Kaikoura, and Applejack Poet also wanting cover, the position he needs will be hard to secure; the STYLE_FIT tag (0.92) reflects that this race shape is not built around him.

runners_data.name: Applejack Poet
runners_data.note: Barry John Murphy has sent out 3 winners from 7 in the last 14 days, which is a live yard angle, and the horse returns only 12 days after his last run — freshness is not the issue; however, a 0W3P record on sim-going, form figures of 84F7-3, and the fact that the hold-up ground he wants at the back is already congested means the redistribution to midfield is a real positional compromise that dims his claims.

races.paceDynamic: Granny Hawkins is the one confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner field and, with no genuine rival to push her along, she is set to dictate from the front at a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good ground over 2m½f at Market Rasen. Tilehurst and Diesel Line will press for prominent positions behind her, creating a small, organised lead group that sets a measured tempo — the kind that keeps the race together and rarely produces dramatic late swoops. Fidendum, Kaikoura, Crown Of India, and Applejack Poet are natural hold-up horses, but Crown Of India and Applejack Poet have been redistributed to midfield on the map because the field's rear is already crowded with genuine closers; neither is likely to secure the position their natural style demands, reducing the credibility of any deep late-finishing move from that quarter. This shape — a single uncontested leader setting an honest but unforced pace — classically favours horses who can travel prominently and pounce in the straight, with genuine hold-up horses who do get the split also capable if the pace proves just quick enough to string the field out.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Granny Hawkins Controls, Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Granny Hawkins leads uncontested at a fair but unhurried clip and the race is decided in the final two flights.
scenarios.body: Granny Hawkins sets the fractions she wants, the pace is controlled enough to favour those tracking her, and Tilehurst or Diesel Line — both positioned to pounce — land the blow in the closing stages; Fidendum, as the most credible hold-up type, is the main threat from further back if she gets daylight early enough.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Fidendum Closes From Off Pace
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just strong enough to string the field out and Fidendum gets a clear run from the hold-up position she favours.
scenarios.body: Nick Slatter (claiming 3lb) is a factor given the weight advantage, and Fidendum's sim-going record of 1W2P on Good and recent placed efforts over the same course and distance give her legitimate claims; she needs more early zip from the front to set up a sustained finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Leader Outstays
scenarios.trigger: If Granny Hawkins slows the race to a crawl, sets it up as a sprint, and uses superior jumping and fitness to win a steadily-run test of concentration.
scenarios.body: With 77 days off the track, Alan King's mare returns to a trip and going where she has won three times, and a truly dawdling pace might expose the rawness of younger rivals like Kaikoura; Tilehurst becomes the biggest danger if she travels fluently throughout.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and Crown Of India or Applejack Poet manage to find their true deep position despite the redistribution pressure.
scenarios.body: Both carry STYLE_FIT discounts and are unlikely to fully secure their natural hold-up berth in this race shape, so this scenario requires an unusually strong tempo that few signs point to on Good ground with a single front-runner; Applejack Poet's trainer has a strong 14-day strike rate but the horse's form figures of 84F7-3 undermine confidence.

watchPoints.text: Watch Granny Hawkins at the start — if she doesn't jump cleanly and establish the lead immediately, the race shape collapses and Tilehurst or Diesel Line could take over the front, fundamentally altering who the race suits.

Kaikoura returns after 267 days off the track; a fit rival that settles in midfield and quickens will quickly expose whether this 4-year-old is race-ready, and a sluggish early move from him under Nathan Moscrop could block the path of Fidendum coming through.

Monitor whether Crown Of India and Applejack Poet can genuinely find cover at the rear — if both are forced to race closer to midfield than they want, neither will produce their optimum finish, reducing the credibility of any late closers' move in the straight.

Diesel Line's last run ended in a fall — watch his jumping through the early flights to establish whether confidence is intact, as a novicey jump or a hesitation will cost him crucial ground in a race run at a contained pace where every length matters.

The 3lb claim of Nick Slatter on Fidendum is notable in a handicap where OR differences are compressed between 89 and 112 — if Fidendum travels smoothly in the hold-up position she wants, the weight relief could be the marginal factor between placed and winning.

races.name: Stay At The Market Rasen Racecourse Caravan Park Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Beny Nahar Road
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist for Henry Hogarth and Jamie Hamilton, 22 days since last run, solid good-ground record (12/15) but needs others to force a strong pace over this 2m7f trip; fell last time out which merits watching at the fences.

runners_data.name: I Am Spider Man
runners_data.note: Barry John Murphy in good recent form (3/7 over 14 days), consistent hold-up performer with three placed finishes at 2m6f on Good last four starts, 12 days since last run is fresh enough; needs a strong pace to deliver his late effort but has the profile if the race is truly run.

runners_data.name: Lunar Morning
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front runner, yet tagged with a 0.90 style-fit discount as this horse has generally raced prominently rather than making all; visor-wearing 5-year-old for Max Comley, 16 days since last run, limited experience (3 runs in hist) means stamina for 2m7f on Good is not fully proven.

runners_data.name: Indian Sunbird
runners_data.note: Strong each-way profile for Sara Ender — impeccable 15/15 Good-ground record and has won over 2m5f at this track; Harry Bannister has a clear map of how to use this horse from a prominent position, trainer slightly lean at 0/6 over 14 days but the horse's own form speaks loudly.

runners_data.name: Jack The Savage
runners_data.note: Won over 2m6f Good last time out for Laura Horsfall and Sean Bowen, who is a major asset; tongue-strap in use, 13/15 on Good ground and a double at this sort of trip in recent history makes him the hold-up horse with most form behind him in this field.

runners_data.name: Copper Beach
runners_data.note: Consistent place-getter (0W5P in hist) for the Parkinson-Smith yard, 7lb claimer Oscar Palmer takes the ride; prominent style suits the anticipated race shape but inability to win from this position is a concern at OR 94 with five recent seconds.

runners_data.name: Larkfield Lusive
runners_data.note: Recent winner (1/24f/GOO) for L J Morgan and Brian Hughes in good nick, prominent style perfectly suits a single front runner scenario; hood-wearing 7-year-old with 10/15 on Good, 33 days since last run is the most significant query but Good ground form is solid.

runners_data.name: You Did
runners_data.note: 150-day absence is a serious flag for Brian Ellison's 6-year-old — all recent winning form on Soft; prominent style suits the expected shape in principle but the long layoff on a switch to Good ground makes form assessment unreliable; hood in use.

runners_data.name: Matoury
runners_data.note: William Maggs (3lb claimer) takes the ride for Mike Sowersby, won last time over 2m3f Good, 16 days since; natural hold-up type who needs the race to develop late, tongue-strap fitted, handles Good well (11/15) but stepping up to 2m7f is an unconfirmed ask.

runners_data.name: Star Vantage
runners_data.note: Rebecca Menzies sends out this 9-year-old whose true running style is hold-up, but with multiple confirmed hold-up horses in the field it is unlikely to find its natural position at the rear; four consecutive fourths in recent form suggest a horse that runs consistently without winning, OR 82.

runners_data.name: The Roc Hopper
runners_data.note: Nathan Moscrop takes the mount on this 7-year-old whose natural hold-up tendency means it is squeezed into a busier midfield than it prefers; limited Good-ground evidence (2/9) compared to Soft specialists in the form string, and a 41-day absence adds further uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Ramaah
runners_data.note: Sarah-Jayne Davies's 5-year-old holds a natural hold-up style but with the rear of the field congested, space may not materialise; visor fitted, all five career runs shown are at shorter trips (2m1f–2m3f) so stamina for 2m7f is genuinely unproven, OR 76 is the lowest weight carrier.

races.paceDynamic: Lunar Morning is the lone confirmed front runner in this 12-runner 2m7f handicap hurdle and, with no genuine rival to press them from the off, Tom Broughton's mount is set to control tempo from the front on Good ground — a sustainable, owner-dictated gallop rather than a pressured one. With Indian Sunbird and Larkfield Lusive likely to sit close behind and Copper Beach also prominent, there will be a small cluster disputing the early positions, but none carries the same front-running intent as Lunar Morning. At 2m7f on Good ground with one uncontested leader, this shape strongly favours prominent-to-midfield types who travel economically in the slipstream and produce a sustained late effort — pure hold-up finishers face a stiff ask because the gallop, though honest, will not be brutally searching. The field does hold more genuine hold-up runners than the map can accommodate at the rear — Star Vantage, The Roc Hopper, and Ramaah are all true hold-up horses who will be competing for a limited number of tracking positions, with Indian Sunbird and Larkfield Lusive best placed to secure their natural prominent roles.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Lunar Morning dictates an uncontested, even gallop and the prominent trackers conserve energy to challenge from the second-last.
scenarios.body: Lunar Morning sets a measured pace that suits the chasers behind, and those who travel prominently without exertion hit the front with momentum intact turning for home; this shape rewards patient, prominent racing at a stiff 2m7f on Good ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Through
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group sets a truly honest gallop and the best-credentialed hold-up runners find a clear run to finish powerfully.
scenarios.body: A genuine pace at this trip stretches the field enough for a horse coming off the bridle from midfield to mow down tired leaders; I Am Spider Man and Jack The Savage have the form and class to deliver this, with Jack The Savage carrying strong recent winning form at 2m6f on Good.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Late Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Lunar Morning sets too slow a gallop early, bunching the field, and the race becomes a sprint finish off a crawl.
scenarios.body: A messy, compressed shape developing late means runners with finishing speed and low weight or a senior jockey's positional nous benefit most; Matoury and Ramaah are lower-rated but lightly weighted and could exploit a race that falls apart tactically.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens, Front Endures
scenarios.trigger: If Lunar Morning is pushed along early by Indian Sunbird or Copper Beach and the pace is genuinely strong throughout the 2m7f trip.
scenarios.body: A strong honest gallop from the front suits a horse with stamina to stay on relentlessly over the full trip; Indian Sunbird's 15/15 good-ground record and consistent placed form at this sort of distance make her the prime candidate to outstay rivals if the pace is punishing.

watchPoints.text: Lunar Morning must be tracked from the flag — if they are swamped early by Indian Sunbird or Larkfield Lusive and lose the front, the entire pace map resets and the race becomes unpredictable.
Jack The Savage with Sean Bowen is a live danger if he gets a clear run from midfield in the straight — he won this trip last time and the jockey will know exactly when to deliver him.
Indian Sunbird's 15/15 Good-ground record is exceptional but trainer Sara Ender is 0/6 over the last 14 days — watch whether that stable form is a coincidence or a pattern heading into this race.

You Did has been off 150 days and all form is on Soft — watch the market closely in the hour before the race; if money comes, the yard is confident; if the price drifts, the absence and going switch are clearly a concern.

Star Vantage, The Roc Hopper and Ramaah are all genuine hold-up horses competing for the same ground at the rear — watch the early positions for crowding and note which, if any, ends up pushed wider or forward than intended, as that positional compromise will shape their finishing chance.

races.name: Sun Racing Summer Jumps Championship Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Fringill Dike
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse trained by Jedd O'Keeffe whose trainer has a sharp 2/2 strike rate over the past 14 days; arrives 23 days fresh, has won this trip on Good going, and his sim-going record of 13/15 with 2 wins and 3 places on Good makes him the standout course-condition fit, though he needs cover and a genuinely run race to deploy his finishing kick.|

runners_data.name: Authorised Speed
runners_data.note: Returns from a massive 785-day absence for Gary & Josh Moore, whose yard is 5/37 in the last 14 days — the primary concern here; carries a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.91 as a natural front runner, but the extended layoff makes this an enormous fitness leap and any physical weakness would be exposed in the closing stages of this 2m5½f test.|

runners_data.name: Regal Renaissance
runners_data.note: In-form prominent racer who has won consecutive starts at Huntingdon and Ayr on Good ground, giving Sean Bowen a horse brimming with confidence; the trip steps up from 2m4f but his Good-ground form and progressive profile make him the dangers on current form, and he will be close enough throughout to pounce if the pace collapses.|

runners_data.name: Gateau De Miel
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Fergal O'Brien who races off a low OR of 114, wears a tongue tie, and has run just 16 days ago suggesting yard freshness is maintained; his 2W4P record on similar going is solid, but at age 10 and from the rear, he needs things to go perfectly in a small field where bunching is likely, making him reliant on a truly decisive late move.|

races.paceDynamic: Authorised Speed is the lone confirmed front runner in this four-runner field and, with no credible challenger for the lead, will control the gallop from the outset at Market Rasen over 2m5½f on Good ground. Fringill Dike and Gateau De Miel are both hold-up types by style, leaving Regal Renaissance as the only prominent-running alternative, though Regal Renaissance is more likely to track than to press hard for the lead. The result is a race where Authorised Speed sets a sustainable, uncontested tempo with no rival willing to make it a test of stamina — the pace will not be a true gallop, and the field will likely travel in a tight bunch until the home turn. This shape strongly favours hold-up horses with a sharp late turn of foot who can exploit a modest fractions-set race, with Fringill Dike and Gateau De Miel best positioned to pounce if the pace is insufficiently strong to string the field out.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Authorised Speed sets an uncontested, conservative gallop that compresses the field and sets up a sprint finish from two out.
scenarios.body: Authorised Speed dictates from the front without pressure, keeping fractions modest and ensuring the race is truly run as a hunt until the home straight; the hold-up horses can then produce their finishing efforts on equal terms. Fringill Dike and Gateau De Miel, both natural closers with good records on Good ground, are best suited to exploit a bunched late dash.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Asserts
scenarios.trigger: If Regal Renaissance travels prominently and challenges Authorised Speed for the lead, creating a genuine end-to-end gallop that tests stamina.
scenarios.body: Regal Renaissance has won two of his last two starts and arrives in the form of his life, and if Sean Bowen elects to press Authorised Speed rather than track, the pace becomes truly searching over this 2m5½f trip. A stronger gallop would favour a prominent racer with strong recent form, and Regal Renaissance's two consecutive wins suggest the stamina is firmly in place.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Misses Break
scenarios.trigger: If the modest pace results in a muddling, messy affair where hold-up horses are caught flat-footed at a crucial stage.
scenarios.body: With only four runners, gaps can close quickly at a false pace and a rider who misjudges the tempo may find rivals already committed when the race ignites; Gateau De Miel, who carries a tongue tie and is aged 10, is the most vulnerable to this risk. Regal Renaissance, already on the premises throughout, would capitalise most cleanly if the closers fail to get a clear run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Authorised Speed Fades Badly
scenarios.trigger: If Authorised Speed, absent 785 days and having raced out of role at a prominent tag rather than its true front-running base, weakens sharply from three out.
scenarios.body: A return from over two years off is a severe ask and if fitness proves insufficient, Authorised Speed will fold turning for home, leaving the race wide open for those tracking behind; the first move on the turn would then be decisive. Regal Renaissance, closest to the pace, and Fringill Dike, motoring through from hold-up, are most likely to benefit from an unexpected implosion at the front.

watchPoints.text: Authorised Speed's 785-day absence is a critical red flag — watch for signs of greenness, laboured jumping, or sudden fading from three out that would entirely reshape the finish.

Regal Renaissance may press Authorised Speed rather than track if Sean Bowen judges the pace too slow; monitor the opening half-mile to see whether this becomes a genuine contest for the lead and transforms the pace scenario.

Gateau De Miel's tongue tie and age (10) in a small-field race where the gallop may be falsely steady could leave Tom Broughton (3) with nowhere to go if rivals quicken sooner than expected — watch his position at the top of the home straight.

With only four runners on Good ground at Market Rasen over 2m5½f, the race is likely to travel in a tight pack until the final bend; any jumping error from any horse — particularly Authorised Speed on his first start in over two years — could trigger a significant positional reshuffle at a critical moment.
Fringill Dike's trainer Jedd O'Keeffe is 2/2 in the last 14 days, a small but 100% strike rate that warrants monitoring as a potential stable confidence indicator heading into this race.

runners_data.name: Ballydisco
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up operator for Tom Lacey with Sean Sheppard aboard; 42 days off but has shown solid Good-ground form (two placings from five recent runs at similar going), tongue strap in play, trips to 28f suggest stamina is not an issue at 3m, though getting back to winning ways from OR 105 asks plenty.

runners_data.name: Zestful Hope
runners_data.note: Charlie Longsdon's nine-year-old is another natural rear-of-field type, with five consecutive runs showing only one win from 15 on comparable going — consistent but not commanding; 32 days off, cheekpieces on, and the drop in class to OR 102 gives a marginal edge.

runners_data.name: Ribeye
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner who sets the entire shape of this race; 64 days off is a flag for an 11-year-old, and the STYLE_FIT tag (0.93) reminds that he has often raced more prominently than he led — if he fails to assert fully he loses his key advantage, but on a sound surface at a flat-jumping track his best chance is to pinch it from the front.

runners_data.name: Queens Wish
runners_data.note: Robert Dunne partners a horse who has been relentlessly consistent — five placings from five recent Good-ground runs — and who sits in a true hold-up position; at OR 94 she carries a realistic weight and her record at 24-26f on Good ground (11 from 15 relevant runs in frame) makes her the quintessential place-the-shape horse here.

runners_data.name: Galway Reel
runners_data.note: Ian Williams saddles Sean Bowen, which is always notable; this horse's natural style is genuine hold-up, but with so many closers in the field it has been pushed forward on the map — Bowen may be able to find a better position than the map suggests, and with 14 from 15 runs on comparable going in frame, the conditions suit perfectly.

runners_data.name: Just A Memory
runners_data.note: Fergal O'Brien's seven-year-old returned to form with back-to-back placings last time out — a 2nd and 3rd — and carries OR 91 with Liam Harrison; a natural hold-up type displaced to midfield by the field's composition, it needs Good ground (only 5 from 15 relevant runs in frame) and a truly run race to threaten.

runners_data.name: Friends Don't Ask
runners_data.note: Clare Ellam's 11-year-old ran only nine days ago — a positive freshness angle or a fatigue concern — and has an excellent record at 24-26f on Good ground (13 from 15 in frame); cheekpieces on, a natural hold-up horse that has found a way into the frame with remarkable regularity, though Charlie Maggs' 3lb claim provides slight weight relief.

runners_data.name: Huckleberry Sting
runners_data.note: A genuine prominent racer who won at 24f on Good ground three runs ago and placed in two subsequent starts; tongue tie applied, 26 days since last run, and Jack Andrews keeps the ride — if Ribeye weakens late, this seven-year-old at OR 84 is the most naturally positioned horse to inherit the race from close order.

runners_data.name: On The Platform
runners_data.note: Belinda Clarke's 10-year-old is prominent in style and returns after 50 days off; the form string includes a win and a pull-up at this trip profile, cheekpieces on, and with only 7 from 15 on comparable going in frame the Good ground is not a concern but consistency is — best treated as an each-way outsider in this shape.

races.paceDynamic: Ribeye is the sole confirmed front-runner in a nine-runner field and, crucially, faces no meaningful pace pressure — with Huckleberry Sting and On The Platform as the only other prominent-style horses, neither is likely to pressurise Ribeye into an unsustainable gallop over 3 miles on Good ground. This sets up a controlled, measured tempo where Ribeye can dictate from the front, conserve energy jumping, and potentially stretch rivals at the second-last when stamina tests begin. The field contains a glut of genuine hold-up horses — Galway Reel, Just A Memory, and Friends Don't Ask are all natural rear-of-field types who have been redistributed to midfield on the map simply because there are more hold-up horses than the race shape can realistically place at the back; Galway Reel and Queenside Wish are most likely to actually settle close enough to strike. The tactical verdict is clear: a solo front-runner setting a sustainable pace on Good ground over 3 miles at Market Rasen strongly favours prominent-to-midfield chasers who can track the gallop and pounce from a close-order position, rather than hold-up horses forced to close excessive ground late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ribeye controls, closers chase
scenarios.trigger: If Ribeye leads at a measured pace and the genuine hold-up horses fail to get early cover, leaving midfield chasers to strike.
scenarios.body: Ribeye sets an uncontested tempo, and by the home straight the horses who tracked closest — Queens Wish and Galway Reel — have the positional advantage to challenge; horses asked to make up ground from the rear find the steady pace insufficient to close the gap.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Held-up closers get through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow in the middle mile, bunching the field and allowing hold-up horses to travel through on the bridle late.
scenarios.body: A crawl through the back straight compresses the field, giving Galway Reel and Just A Memory a realistic chance to come from off the pace without needing exceptional late dash; the final-fence scramble suits those who have been conserving energy all race.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Ribeye fades, prominent pair inherit
scenarios.trigger: If Ribeye's front-running effort takes its toll over the final mile and the two genuine prominent types Huckleberry Sting and On The Platform move through.
scenarios.body: Ribeye's age (11) and a 64-day absence create stamina uncertainty in the final third of the race, and if it weakens from two out, Huckleberry Sting — who has winning form at this course and distance profile and has been in fine recent form — is ideally placed to inherit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-up horse surprises
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entirely in the back straight, creating a falsely run race that suits a stayer grinding late from the rear.
scenarios.body: Ballydisco or Zestful Hope, both genuine hold-up types with sound Good-ground form, get a soft lead to chase and grind out a late challenge; however, the redistribution of so many natural hold-up horses into midfield means the race is likely to be competitive enough in the middle to prevent a true late-closers' romp.

watchPoints.text: Ribeye's absence of 64 days at age 11 is the single biggest variable — if he jumps lethargically or weakens before two out, the entire SCENARIO_A framework collapses and Huckleberry Sting becomes the immediate beneficiary of positional advantage.

Galway Reel with Sean Bowen is a combination capable of outrunning its mapped position — watch whether Bowen moves forward from the off, which would tighten the shape and convert a SCENARIO_B outcome into a closer's contest.

Friends Don't Ask ran just nine days ago; watch the pre-race market and paddock for any sign of fatigue — if it shortens despite a tight turnaround, Ellam clearly believes it has bounced out of the previous run well.

Queens Wish has placed in seven of her last eleven Good-ground runs but has not won at OR 94 — watch whether Robert Dunne commits for a challenge earlier than usual, because her style requires a strongly run race to deliver a winning effort rather than another near-miss.

The cluster of natural hold-up horses (Ballydisco, Zestful Hope, Galway Reel, Just A Memory, Friends Don't Ask) all seeking similar ground at the rear means significant positional congestion is likely in the back straight — early scrimmaging for cover could unsettle one or more of these runners and create a race incident worth noting for future assessments.
